tier_reason: README Performance table (seq 1024: 1.1-2.0x, 2048: 1.7-3.7x, 4096: 2.0-3.9x, 8192+: 3-4x vs PyTorch SDPA; 'Average speedup: 1.8x') matches the record, but it is first-party, gives ranges only, and names no chip ('Apple Silicon (M1/M2/M3/M4/M5)'), macOS, torch version or raw timings; the public harnesses (test_benchmark.py, mps_flash_attn/benchmark.py) are not tied to the table, so C.

corrections.stars_or_usage: 14 stars, 3 forks (github.com page now shows mpsops/mps-flash-attention); PyPI package mps-flash-attn 0.6.3 uploaded 2026-09-01
corrections.caveats: First-party tier C: the README table gives speedup ranges per sequence length ('Benchmarked on Apple Silicon (M1/M2/M3/M4/M5)') with no per-chip, dtype, head-dim, batch or torch-version breakdown and no raw timings; it calls 1024 the 'crossover point', so shorter sequences (512 is in the harness) are not claimed faster. The harnesses are public: test_benchmark.py (B=1, H=8, D=64, float16, N 512-8192, 3 warmup and 10 timed runs, torch.mps.synchronize after every call) and mps_flash_attn/benchmark.py (5 warmup and 20 runs with one synchronize after the loop, fp16/bf16, batch 1 and 4, head dim 64 and 128, causal variants, plus an output-difference check against SDPA; its memory figure is a current_allocated_memory delta, not peak memory). Both sides call the real F.scaled_dot_product_attention (no patched SDPA in the harness). The baseline is PyTorch's own MPS SDPA path, which materialises the N x N attention matrix (hence the OOMs at 8192+), so the win is against a non-flash baseline. Kernel speed comes from metal-flash-attention, already listed as philipturner/metal-flash-attention: this package is a PyTorch C++ extension plus Swift bridge over imperatormk/metal-flash-attention (an MIT-licensed fork of philipturner/metal-flash-attention, 175 commits on its causal branch) and no comparison against plain MFA is given. The repository now lives at mpsops/mps-flash-attention: the imperatormk URL resolves to that page, and the README clone URL and PyPI project URLs point there. TODO.md is a stale planning file whose boxes (including 'Performance benchmarks vs naive MPS attention') are all unchecked although those features ship.

tier_reason: Peer-reviewed TCHES 2026 paper (ePrint 2026/947; Ganqin Liu, Hao Cheng, Georgios Fotiadis, Jipeng Zhang, Johann Großschädl) reports the AVX-512 BLS software at least 1.57x faster than blst x64 assembly on an Intel Core i3-1005G1, seen only as search snippets (eprint.iacr.org and iacr.org EGRESS_BLOCKED). The repo has public bench code for both sides (test.c MEASURE_CYCLES rdtsc loops, vendored blst built by build.sh) and makefile flags, but the paper's tables, compiler version and a repo-to-paper link could not be read, so B not A; upgraded from C for consistency with hchengv/avxbls (B on a TCHES snippet).

corrections.claimed_speedup: Repository publishes no numbers (test.c prints scalar/baseline versus vec average cycles at run time). Paper 'Efficient SIMD Implementation of the BLS Signature Scheme Using Intel AVX-512' (TCHES 2026, ePrint 2026/947; abstract seen as a WebSearch snippet only): the vectorised BLS software using AVX-512 (AVX-512IFMA, 8-way 52x52-bit multiplies) is at least 1.57 times faster than an x64 assembly implementation of blst, benchmarked on an Intel Core i3-1005G1 (Ice Lake). Per-operation figures not read.
corrections.caveats: Tier B rests on search snippets of the paper abstract (TCHES 2026, ePrint 2026/947), not on the paper itself: eprint.iacr.org and iacr.org are blocked here, so the per-operation cycle tables, the compiler version used and turbo settings were not read, and the 'at least 1.57x' lower bound cannot be mapped to specific operations. The repo README has no paper link; the link is inferred from the matching first author (Ganqin Liu, repo owner) and topic. test.c averages rdtsc (reference cycles, not core cycles) over 10,000-100,000 iterations after a 1,000-iteration warm-up, for scalar multiplication, point add/double, isogeny maps, sk_to_pk, subgroup checks, hash-to-curve, signing in G1 and G2, pairing aggregation (blst_pairing_chk_n_mul_n_aggr_pk_in_g1/g2), core verify and final verify. The baseline is the single-signature blst API built from a vendored blst copy (src_blst/server.c plus build_blst/assembly.S via build.sh: -O3 -fno-builtin -fPIC, -D__ADX__ when the CPU has ADX, -mno-avx), not blst's multi-threaded or batch-verification paths. The signing benchmarks hash with SwiftEC (blst_swiftec_* from src/swiftec_blst.c, the authors' addition, not part of upstream blst) when the SWIFTEC_ON switch is set and with standard blst_hash_to_g1/g2 otherwise; where SWIFTEC_ON is defined was not located. A prebuilt libblst.a binary is committed and the makefile hard-codes /opt/gcc-13.3/bin/gcc. The pairing code builds on hchengv/avxbls (already listed, tier B), so verification gains overlap that entry. Needs AVX-512 IFMA (Ice Lake or newer). Retier to A if the paper names the compiler and flags matching the makefile.

notes: Repo has bench code but no numbers; paper claim (>=1.57x vs blst on i3-1005G1, TCHES 2026) from two WebSearch snippets only, ePrint and iacr.org EGRESS_BLOCKED (one try each). Metadata confirmed on github.com: Apache-2.0 (LICENSE read), 0 stars, 0 forks, not a fork, 22 commits, last commit 2026-03-12 (active). Distinct from hchengv/avxbls (signature scheme vs pairing) but reuses its pairing code; benchmark_url set to the ePrint page found by search (not openable here).

tier_reason: The only ratio is the first-party bbuhrow/avx-ecm README sentence ('about 1.5 to 2.5 times the throughput (curves/sec) of GMP-ECM, for numbers up to a thousand bits or so', 'has been observed') with no CPU, compiler, flags, B1/B2, GMP-ECM version or benchmark script; the YAFU README, wiki and docfile.txt carry no comparison against GMP-ECM, msieve or CADO-NFS, so C.

corrections.caveats: Weak evidence for the listed baseline. (1) The YAFU README has no baseline comparison; it says only that on AVX-512 CPUs YAFU uses AVX-ECM as the default built-in ECM backend and that a standalone version lives at bbuhrow/avx-ecm. The only GMP-ECM ratio is the first-party 'has been observed' sentence in that standalone repo (BSD-2-Clause, 8 stars, last commit 2021-03-09), already listed as its own entry, with no CPU, compiler, flags, B1/B2 bounds, GMP-ECM version or benchmark code; YAFU's in-tree AVX-ECM has been developed further since (IFMA builds), so the 2021-era ratio may not describe the current backend in either direction. (2) The YAFU wiki Benchmarks page (https://github.com/bbuhrow/yafu/wiki/Benchmarks) has SIQS-only wall-clock tables per CPU, OS, compiler (GCC 11.4-16.1, Clang 17.0.6 and 21.0.0), ISA label and thread count (for example AMD Ryzen 9 5950X, GCC 13.3, AVX2 BMI2, 16 threads: 10.22 s sieve, 13.17 s total at 85 digits) but no msieve, GMP-ECM or CADO-NFS column; no other wiki page or docfile.txt section compares against an external tool. (3) WebSearch snippets of mersenneforum threads (pages blocked, not opened; snippet only) say YAFU SIQS was faster than msieve QS on old versions (a yafu-1.0 vs msieve-1.38 table with 0.97x-1.55x for 50-85 digits; another 85-digit table with 386 s versus 873 s); those 2008-2010 numbers are not recorded as evidence. (4) No NFS comparison against CADO-NFS was found. (5) Licence: no LICENSE, LICENSE.txt or COPYING file (all 404); the public-domain dedication is a source header (top/driver.c: 'placed in the public domain by its author, Ben Buhrow'), no patent grant; bundled components (msieve, ytools, ysieve, zlib, GGNFS siever binaries, CUDA kernels) keep their own terms and optional GMP/GMP-ECM linking brings LGPL/GPL obligations, hence 'mixed'.

notes: avx-ecm README sentence matches the record; YAFU README, wiki index, wiki Benchmarks page and docfile.txt checked: no external comparison. Metadata confirmed on github.com: 381 stars, 54 forks, 989 commits, no licence file, last commit 2026-10-05 (active).
